title: Forerunners within the prophet lineage
statement: Within the prophet sequence of woh-claim-0038, the corpus distinguishes a preparatory sub-class — forerunners, whose missions prepare the way for a more central figure (John the Baptist before Jesus as the type case) — inside the roughly forty-prophet lineage the corpus tracks, distinct from the age-inaugural prophets; the sub-classification is corpus systematization over the sequence, at speculative grade.

includes: The functional distinction: preparatory missions versus age-inaugural ones, with John the Baptist as the canon-adjacent type case
The lineage frame: the roughly forty-prophet count as the corpus's tracking construct over the sequence, disclosed as such
The dependency discipline: everything here rides on woh-claim-0038; a forerunner is a sequence member with a preparatory tasking, nothing more
excludes: Canonical status for the sub-class; the canon names figures and missions, and the class is the corpus's sorting
Membership adjudication beyond figures the corpus has actually classed
The forty-count as canon-stated arithmetic; it is the corpus's census of its own tracking
Any figure outside the sequence's own scope rules

source_references.locator: The prophet-mission material the sub-classification sorts
Mark 1:2-8 (MARK-WOH-1:2-8 in the in-house rendering): the messenger preparing the way — the type case's textual basis

alternatives.statement: The forerunner category is the gospels' own Elijah-typology for the Baptist; the corpus generalizes a Christian literary frame into an operational class.
Preparatory-versus-inaugural is the corpus's sorting convenience; no tasking distinction exists in the sources.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0038 is revised or retired.
The corpus's lineage tracking changes the census or the classing.
Public prose begins asserting canonical status for the class or adjudicating unclassed figures, both of which this record excludes.
